name: Shiva (Shiva Ka Insaaf)
summary: Jackie Shroff's masked crusader from the 1985 Hindi film Shiva Ka Insaaf: an orphan trained by three father figures, billed as the first Hindi film shot in 3D.
origin: Bhola's parents are killed by the crime boss Jagan. Three men, Ram, Rahim and Robert, bring him up and train him as a fighter. In the film they take him to a Shiva temple, rename him Shiva and tell him the god's strength will flow through him. He works as a newspaper reporter in the city and fights Jagan's gang as the masked hero Shiva, winning public fame while Jagan hunts for his identity.
powers: Caped costume and a ring that mark him as Shiva
Trained in combat by three father figures

storyline.title: A family lost
storyline.beat: Jagan has Bhola's parents killed, and three older men take the boy in and raise him together.

storyline.title: Becoming Shiva
storyline.beat: The three guardians train Bhola in fighting, take him to a Shiva temple, and give him a costume, ring and weapons. He takes the name Shiva.

storyline.title: Reporter by day
storyline.beat: Bhola works at Jagan's newspaper as a journalist, meets Nisha, and defeats Jagan's bandits as the masked Shiva.

storyline.title: The orphanage threat
storyline.beat: Jagan threatens to bomb an orphanage unless Shiva dies. The hero recovers from a near-fatal attack and stops the plot with his guardians.

gossip.text: R. D. Burman composed the soundtrack and Kader Khan wrote the dialogues.
Its 3D scenes were built around objects flying toward the audience, such as steel balls kicked at the screen.
Poonam Dhillon plays Nisha and Shakti Kapoor plays the villain Jagan.
The film is now often watched for laughs, but at release it was seen as a glimpse of where Indian cinema was heading.

quiz.q: Which uncle kicks steel balls toward the audience in the 3D scene?
quiz.why: Robert kicks steel balls with great accuracy, so they seem to fly out of the screen.

quiz.q: Which actor plays Bhola, who becomes Shiva?
quiz.why: Jackie Shroff plays Bhola and Shiva.

quiz.q: What is the film best known for in Hindi cinema?
options: First Hindi film with a robot hero
First Hindi film with talking animals
quiz.why: It is termed the first Hindi film made in 3D.

theme.tagline: A cape, a ring and a 3D leap before Indian cinema had CGI.

timeline.title: Shiva in 3D
timeline.note: Jackie Shroff's masked hero arrives in Raj N. Sippy's film, billed as the first Hindi 3D release.

timeline.title: Sound award
timeline.note: The 33rd Filmfare Awards, covering 1985 films, give the film its Best Sound award.

timeline.title: Son flies too
timeline.note: Jackie's son Tiger Shroff stars in A Flying Jatt, and writers look back at his father's earlier superhero role.

timeline.title: A remake wish
timeline.note: Tiger Shroff says in April 2017 that he would like to play the superhero if his father's film were ever remade.

facts.text: It was not India's first 3D film. The Malayalam children's film My Dear Kuttichathan, released in August 1984, is the one usually given that title.
Bhola's dying father tells him to find three men listed with photos in a diary. Ram, Rahim and Robert turn out to be a jolly trio who live together and raise and train the boy.
The 3D showpiece is a scene where the uncle Robert kicks steel balls with accuracy straight at the audience, so they seem to fly out of the screen.
A DailyO reviewer says one godown scene, in which cars knock over stacked cartons, was clearly shot with toy cars.

In the film, the three uncles take Bhola to a Shiva temple, rename him Shiva and give him a black cape with a trident emblem and a ring bearing the eye of Shiva, telling him the warrior god's strength will flow through him.
Each uncle has a signature weapon skill: Ram spins a pair of sticks at speed, Robert kicks steel balls with precision, and Rahim is skilled with a whip.
On his first mission to free villagers from bandits, Shiva uses a sword to shave off the villains' hair, beards and moustaches into comic shapes.
The film's hero can fly, yet in one scene he chases a car full of baddies on a bicycle, a mismatch between his powers and his transport that DailyO's reviewer pokes fun at.
Vikram, played by Gulshan Grover, puts on Shiva's costume to fool Nisha, until the real Shiva appears, fights him off and unmasks to show her he is Bhola.
The villain Jagan first appears as a horse-riding bandit with a scar on his hand. Young Bhola notices the scar, and the film does not show it again until the final showdown.
In the city, Bhola disguises himself with oversized glasses and a dim-witted manner, so nobody suspects the bumbling newcomer is the masked hero that crowds love.
Jagan's son Vikram, played by Gulshan Grover, is the city's crime lord and also pursues the heroine, so the hero has a rival as well as the father who murdered his parents.
The hero carries a trident and a sword, throws tridents, leaps to great heights and flies, though a DailyO reviewer says the effects look basic.
Jackie Shroff plays Shiva as a permanently grinning hero. DailyO's reviewer calls the film nonstop silliness, though it was seen as a glimpse of the future when it came out.
The two sources disagree on a detail: Wikipedia says Jagan owns the newspaper and the heroine is called Nisha, while DailyO says the paper is run by the heroine, whom it calls Rekha.
The heroine, played by Poonam Dhillon, falls for the masked Shiva without realising he is also the clumsy colleague Bhola whom she works with every day.
Jagan's plot to blow up the uncles' orphanage forces Shiva's last fight. He is badly wounded into a coma, but he wakes, removes all the bombs and joins the uncles against Jagan's gang.
Wikipedia pages disagree on the release date: the English page gives 15 March 1985, while Simple English Wikipedia, citing the Times of India, gives 22 February 1985.
Simple English Wikipedia describes the hero's powers as coming from his belief in the god Shiva, and calls the film India's first superhero film as well as the first Hindi 3D film.
Jagan is desperate to learn who Shiva really is and offers money to anyone who can reveal the hero's identity, which is why Bhola must keep his comic reporter act convincing.

kidSummary: Shiva is a masked hero in a 1985 Hindi film, the first Hindi film shot in 3D. He is a boy named Bhola, raised and trained by three kind uncles. Shiva is a film hero named after the god, not the god himself.

story.title: Raised by three uncles
story.text: Young Bhola loses his parents. Three kind men named Ram, Rahim and Robert raise him and teach him to fight.

story.title: The new name
story.text: The uncles take him to a Shiva temple, rename him Shiva and give him a black cape and a special ring.

story.title: Bumbling by day
story.text: In the city he plays a clumsy newspaper reporter with thick glasses, and he becomes the masked hero Shiva whenever crime strikes.

story.title: Funny fights
story.text: Shiva uses a sword to shave bandits' beards and moustaches into silly shapes. Robert's steel balls seem to fly out of the screen at the audience in 3D.

story.title: Saving the orphanage
story.text: When the villain Jagan threatens an orphanage, Shiva and his three uncles stop his plan and keep the children safe.
